PullRequest.Title: Align animated menus and action widgets to device pixels
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347796

## What

With Modern UI and motion on, the open animation of title bar menus, context menus and action widgets (for example the chat pickers) could end with some or all rows snapping by one device pixel.

## Why

These surfaces open by animating `transform: scale(0.97 → 1)` on a child of a positioned container. While the transform is active, Chromium paints the content from a pixel-snapped offset. Once the animation ends, it paints the content at its exact device-pixel offset. When the container is on a fractional device pixel, which is common (for example the View menu sits at `top: 28.5px` below the title bar at DPR 1), the two can round rows differently. Rows then move by one device pixel in the frame after the animation finishes.

## How

New helper `DOM.alignToDevicePixels(element, direction?)`:
- It measures the element and nudges its inline px `left`/`top` (or `right`/`bottom` when those are the anchored insets) so the element starts on a whole device pixel.
- It takes into account the window's `devicePixelRatio` and CSS zoom, including zoom on shadow hosts.
- It ignores offsets within Chromium's layout precision (positions are floored to 1/64 CSS px), so calling it again doesn't move the element.

Where it is called:
- **`ContextView.doLayout()`** (context menus, dropdown menus, action widgets) uses the same rounding, but computes it from the geometry it has already measured instead of re-reading layout after writing the position. This matters because some callers (the action widget collapse) lay out every animation frame.
  - The edge that faces the anchor snaps to the nearest device pixel. Chromium paints the anchor's own edge at that same pixel, so the view meets the anchor with no gap and no visible overlap. If the view's rendered size differs from its layout size (zoom or subpixel content), the edge facing the anchor rounds to the anchor's painted edge, not to its own rendered edge. Other edges also round to the nearest device pixel.
  - It works in the rendered (client) coordinates that ContextView uses since #234970, and only converts to CSS pixels when writing the position.
  - Alignment never moves a view past the viewport. A view beside its anchor that is pinned against the viewport edge, or that would cover the window controls overlay, stays unaligned. These checks use the view's rendered position and size, including CSS zoom.
- **`MenuBar.showCustomMenu()`**: keeps the menu's edge that meets the title (its bottom edge when the compact menu opens upwards) on its painted device pixel, so the menu meets the title bar's painted edge.

No animation, timing, easing or reduced-motion behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Live before/after in a Code OSS build**
- Setup: `--force-device-scale-factor`, frosted glass on. The real open animation is held at `scale(0.99999)` while its keyframes still end at `scale(1)`, and that frame is compared with the resting frame.
- "Before" is the same build with the helper as a no-op.

Rows moving at least 0.5 device px:

| Surface | DPR 1 | DPR 1.32 (110 %, zoom 1) | DPR 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| View menu (title bar) | 16 → **0** | 8 → **0** | 0 → 0 |
| Models picker (action widget, same path as the agent picker) | 0 → 0 | 2 → **0** | 0 → 0 |
| Status bar context menu | 0 → 0 | 2 → **0** | 0 → 0 |

- Every container now starts on a whole device pixel and moves at most one device pixel.
- Re-run on the latest revision: 0 jumped rows at DPR 1, 1.32 and 2 for the View menu, Models picker, agent picker and status bar context menu.
- With `workbench.reduceMotion: on`, menus still open without animation.

**Tests**
- **New tests:** in `dom.test.ts`, `contextview.test.ts` and `menubar.test.ts`.
  - They cover fractional positions, rounding direction, views below, above and pinned against the viewport, the compact menubar, CSS and shadow-host zoom, and repeated layout.
  - Placement checks against the anchor compare painted device pixels: with a half-pixel anchor, the view meets the anchor's painted edge while the two layout boxes overlap by half a device pixel.
  - They fail without the fix and pass with it.
  - In the Chromium browser runner, the earlier revision of this PR fails them along with both `TabbedModelPicker` tests that failed CI. This revision passes all of them.
- **Related suites:** dom, ContextView, menu, menubar, dropdown, action widget, model picker, frosted glass and menu motion, run with `scripts/test.bat`. They have the same 28 local failures as `main` (timeouts, two placement assertions, and a window-size case), so this change adds no new failures.
- **Lint and type check:** `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files and `pnpm run typecheck-client` pass.

**Layout cost** (Chromium traces, 25 opens per case at DPR 1, 1.32 and 2, `main` vs. this PR)
- Context menus and action widgets: alignment reads no layout after writing the position. Forced style recalcs and layouts per open match `main` (5 and 4 at every DPR), with no flush attributed to alignment. So the action widget's per-frame `layout()` during its collapse animation costs the same as before.
- Title bar menus: the `Menu` constructor has already laid out, so the read is free and the inset write adds one small layout per open (under 0.1 ms).
- Per-frame style/layout and input-handler time are unchanged within noise.

**GPU compositing path:** this machine has no GPU, so Code OSS was run with Chromium's GPU compositing and GPU raster path on ANGLE's SwiftShader backend (`gpu_compositing: enabled`). "Before" is the same build with `dom.ts`, `contextview.ts` and `menubar.ts` restored to the merge base. The jump reproduces there: View menu 16 rows at DPR 1 and 8 at 1.32, Models picker and status bar context menu 1 row each at 1.32, all by about 1 device px. With the fix, no row moves by half a device pixel or more in any of the four surfaces at DPR 1, 1.32 and 2.

**Not verified:** real GPU hardware and drivers, the default D3D11 ANGLE backend and the macOS and Linux backends; and the agent picker itself, which didn't reproduce here; the Models picker stands in for it.

Full engineering report (plan, reviews, all evidence): https://aka.ms/publish?a=76be22c9-49d8-4b4f-9d4b-e877068f684f

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or relayout a context menu, dropdown, hover, or action widget, including the action-widget body collapse animation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ContextView.show/layout calls doLayout synchronously before the popup can be positioned or each animation frame can settle. Existing anchor, viewport, zoom, and view-size reads remain on this path; the diff computes alignment from those already-read values before writing top/left, so it adds no geometry read or style/layout flush after the writes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser geometry/style/layout reads for the anchor and context view, followed by top/left style writes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One positioning pass per popup open or explicit layout; during a collapsible action-widget animation, one pass per animation frame for the single active context view
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same path reset position, read anchor/view geometry and zoom, ran layout2d and window-controls avoidance, then wrote top/left. It did not device-pixel-adjust the resulting coordinates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous and required before that popup/frame is positioned. The expensive DOM reads pre-date the diff; added alignment is constant-size arithmetic and a bounded number of overlay-clearance checks using already measured geometry.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One visible context view. During animation, cost scales with frame count, not menu rows or repositories; the added work is O(1) per frame with at most a few constant candidate checks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ContextViewService owns one active ContextView, and animation callbacks invoke its layout serially once per animation frame; there is no fan-out or concurrent boundary burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Cold and repeated layouts perform the same bounded alignment arithmetic; repeated alignment does not add retained state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call receives positioningOrigin dimensions and other geometry already read by doLayout, and alignViewToDevicePixels performs only numeric/object operations plus the pure window-controls helper.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser layout duration varies with popup DOM complexity, but the diff introduces no additional layout measurement on this path, so there is no evidenced new scaling or critical-path layout regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The per-frame path gains bounded arithmetic and small short-lived objects but no new synchronous DOM read, boundary call, or collection-scaled work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch a title-bar or compact menubar menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: showCustomMenu constructs and lays out the menu, then the new alignment helper walks the short ancestor chain for CSS zoom, reads the holder rect, and writes adjusted inline insets before focus/open completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Computed-style traversal and getBoundingClientRect for the newly constructed menu holder
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for each opened or keyboard-switched menu; only one menu is active and calls are serialized
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: After constructing the Menu, the code immediately registered handlers and focused it; it did not perform the final zoom/rect read or device-pixel inset adjustment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read is synchronous on menu-open critical path. Menu construction already calls getDomNodeZoomLevel, measures the holder, appends all rows, and scanDomNode reads client/scroll dimensions; the diff adds one final bounded alignment read and inset write rather than per-row or per-frame work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The helper's own style traversal scales with fixed DOM ancestor depth and runs once per opened menu. Browser rect resolution can depend on the constructed menu subtree, but the constructor has already synchronously scanned that same subtree and there is no loop over actions introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active custom menu at a time; opening or switching menus executes synchronously and sequentially with no queued or parallel reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used or needed. Each newly created holder is measured once; repeat calls across separate opens act on new menu DOM.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the new synchronous read exists; high that cardinality is one per menu open/switch and does not fan out. Confidence is low that it causes a material regression because surrounding construction already forces menu measurements.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact cost of the final rect read depends on browser dirty-layout state and menu size. Code evidence shows bounded once-per-open cardinality and an existing constructor layout scan, so there is no concrete evidence of user-visible latency or a meaningful scaling amplification.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added read is bounded and serialized, with no realistic multiplicity or demonstrated material critical-path cost that meets the performance finding threshold.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the newly added device-pixel alignment and placement tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test-only loops and repeated layouts execute only in browser test suites and do not ship on product startup, rendering, input, or menu-open paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Synthetic DPR, position, and placement cases fixed by the tests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No product cache behavior is touched.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from changed-file locations and test-suite declarations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Test runtime may increase, but these tests are not a user-facing product scenario and their loops are bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance regression; test-only work is out of scope for a user-visible finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and all diff pages. Traced context-view open/relayout, the per-frame action-widget animation path, title-bar menu creation/switching, layout/style boundaries, cardinality, caching, and concurrency. The context-view change reuses existing measurements and adds only O(1) arithmetic; the menubar change adds one bounded serialized geometry read per open after existing menu measurements. No actionable diff-introduced performance issue or performance-regression fix was established.
